# Phase 01.1: Design System Migration - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-08-04
**Status:** Ready for planning

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Replace the shadcn visual layer with the imported Cena design system — tokens,
re-skinned Radix primitives, and a token contract separating Cena's product brand
from a themable venue brand — and re-author the surfaces the imported design got
wrong, so every phase from 2 onward designs against a system that matches what
Cena actually is.

This is an **enabling phase**. It delivers no requirement ID directly. It is a
hard prerequisite for THEME-01..04 and supplies the design vocabulary every later
phase's UI-SPEC consumes. It blocks phases 2–7.

**Scope decision, 2026-08-04 — read this before D-02.** **v1 surfaces everything
in Cena's own design, the diner menu included.** Owner/venue UI customization is a
later milestone. This *reverses* the original D-02, which held that Cena's azure
must never touch the diner surface. The revised D-02 below carries the current
direction and the superseded text; D-14 records what 01.1 still builds for the
later theming milestone. Any downstream agent reading only the original D-02 will
design the wrong diner surface.

**A note that changes how this phase must be read.** The research this phase is
built on — `.planning/research/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`, audited 2026-08-02 — went stale
before planning began. The design project was re-read live on 2026-08-04 and had
moved substantially: the brand pivoted from terracotta to Szeged azure, and the
audit's largest blocker (B-2, "the diner surface does not exist") was resolved by
a new `templates/qr-menu/` that did not exist when the audit was written. The
delta is recorded as a dated section at the top of that file. **Downstream agents
must read the delta before the audit body**, or they will plan against a brand and
a gap list that no longer exist.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Brand direction

- **D-01:** Adopt the Szeged-derived palette as Cena's product brand, as-is —
  `szeged` azure (`--szeged-700 #0b5fa5`) primary, `napfeny` gold accent under a
  ~5% per-screen cap, `paprika` destructive, `tisza` as the only neutral. This
  accepts the design project's pivot away from the original written brief
  ("warm feeling, organic, almost Italian"). Rationale: the system is fully
  built, every pair measured to AA in `color-contrast.card.html`, dark mode
  already defined, and it leans into Hungary — which PROJECT.md names the sharper
  wedge because it displaces paper rather than a competitor. Known trade-off
  accepted knowingly: a brand anchored in one city's heraldry is an awkward
  anchor for the EU-general expansion PROJECT.md plans.
  — **Reversibility:** costly — undoing it means re-authoring `tokens/colors.css`,
  all 21 guideline cards, the dark-mode token set and both new templates, plus
  every repo surface re-skinned against it in this phase.

- **D-02 (REVISED 2026-08-04 — supersedes the original):** **v1 renders every
  surface, diner included, in Cena's own design.** Szeged azure, the napfeny gold
  accent under its 5% cap, the Cena type pairing — the diner menu looks like Cena,
  exactly like the owner surfaces do. **Owner/venue customization of the UI is a
  later milestone**, not a v1 capability.

  *Superseded text, kept for the record:* the original D-02 held that Cena's azure
  must not appear on the diner surface at all, and that the diner menu would carry
  the venue's palette and font pairing inside Cena's fixed structure. That was
  reversed by user decision on 2026-08-04.

  **What this resolves.** Research raised an open question the original D-02 could
  not answer: the imported template puts `Badge tone="warning"` (napfeny gold) and
  `Button variant="primary"` (azure) on the diner surface. Under the revised D-02
  those are simply Cena's own colours doing their normal job — **allowed, not a
  violation**. Research's related "raw-ramp leak" finding (`--tisza-100/200` used
  directly rather than through a semantic token) likewise stops being a boundary
  breach; it remains worth normalising for the token layer's own hygiene, but it is
  no longer a correctness issue.

  **What this does not change.** The token *namespace* boundary is still built in
  01.1 — see D-14. It simply has no consumer in v1.
  — **Reversibility:** reversible — v1 ships one brand, so there is no themed
  surface to re-cut. Adding venue theming later reads the boundary D-14 builds.

- **D-03 (scope narrowed by revised D-02):** When venue font choice (THEME-02)
  eventually ships, it is a **small curated set of 3–4 pairings**, every one
  self-hosted and subset for RO/HU diacritics (`ă â î ș ț` / `ő ű`) and
  diacritic-verified before shipping. A Google Fonts picker is ruled out by
  ROADMAP 01.1 SC1 ("no third-party font or asset request on any page"); each
  pairing is bytes on the diner critical path, which DINE-03 makes load-bearing.
  **v1 ships one pairing — Cena's own** (D-09), so this decision now constrains a
  later milestone rather than describing v1 behaviour.

- **D-04:** Keep the voice **register** verbatim — calm floor manager, second
  person active present, sentence case, no emoji, errors state what happened then
  what to do, confirmations past tense with undo. **Re-cut the lexicon** to
  menu-tier words: drop covers, turns, the pass, fired, 86'd, the book, walk-in,
  close out. Additionally close the **six owed Copywriting Contract rows**
  recorded in `01-UAT.md` § "Copywriting Contract — additions from the gap round",
  since 01.1 touches every surface those strings live on.

### Diner design vocabulary

- **D-05:** The new `templates/qr-menu/` self-declares coverage of DINE-02,
  DINE-04, DINE-05, DINE-06, MENU-08, MENU-09, MENU-10, LANG-05, LANG-06,
  THEME-03 and ACCT-02. **That claim is unverified and must be verified before
  it is relied on.** Research verifies the template against each requirement it
  names; 01.1 then adopts the patterns that genuinely hold and authors only the
  residue. Do not convert a template README's self-report into settled fact for
  phases 2–7.

- **D-06:** Vocabulary scope is **the diner surface, plus the unverified-field
  marking state defined at the token/primitive level** — not the whole ingestion
  UI. Rationale: unverified-AI-field marking is a legal release gate under the
  EU food-information constraint in PROJECT.md, it is cheap to define once, and
  leaving Phase 7 to invent it under time pressure is how that gate gets done
  badly. Other owner-side patterns (per-language authoring LANG-01..04, the
  QR print sheet DINE-01) ship with the phases that need them, designed against
  real code.

  **Note a drafting problem in the ROADMAP for whoever owns it:** SC5 lists
  "unverified-AI-field marking" as part of the *diner menu's* vocabulary, but it
  is an owner-side pre-publish concern — the diner never sees it. D-06 honours
  SC5's intent; the wording should be corrected.

- **D-07:** The DINE-04 last-good state is **timestamped and specific** —
  e.g. "Saved menu from 14:20. Prices and sold-out items may have changed."
  Rationale: it follows the system's own rule that errors say what happened then
  what to do, and it serves PROJECT.md's named risk that "a diner orders
  something that has been off for a month and credibility is gone". A bare
  "Saved menu" cannot distinguish five minutes from five weeks.

- **D-08:** The zero-photo state is a **genuinely different, typographic layout**
  — not the photo layout with placeholders in it. Dish name in the serif,
  description, price, allergens, generous spacing, no image slot. Rationale:
  PROJECT.md's Key Decisions give the reason directly — "empty image slots look
  worse than a design that never expected them" — and most independent
  restaurants have no photography, so this is the common case, not the edge case.
  **This overrides the imported template**, whose README currently renders every
  image as a "labelled striped placeholder" while simultaneously claiming the
  zero-photo state is "the design's default, not a degraded mode". Those two
  claims are inconsistent; D-08 resolves it in favour of PROJECT.md.

### Scope boundary of this phase

- **D-09:** Self-host and subset **Cena's own pairing only** in 01.1 — Newsreader,
  Instrument Sans, IBM Plex Mono — and remove the Google Fonts CDN request,
  satisfying SC1 and unblocking the diner surface (W-2). The other 2–3 venue
  pairings ship in **Phase 4** alongside the theming UI that lets a venue pick
  one. Nothing is built before a surface exists to use it.

- **D-10:** Keep the dark-mode token definitions but **wire no dark UI** in 01.1,
  and lock the rule that **the diner menu never follows the device's dark
  preference**. Dark mode appears in no success criterion; the tokens cost nothing
  dormant.

  **Rationale amended 2026-08-04.** The original rationale — "the diner menu
  carries the venue's palette, so auto-darkening would destroy the venue's
  identity" — is void under the revised D-02, since v1's diner menu carries Cena's
  palette. The *decision* is unaffected for 01.1 either way, because no dark UI is
  wired at all. **Flagged for the theming milestone:** whether a Cena-branded diner
  menu should honour `prefers-color-scheme` is now an open question with no
  standing answer. The `token-boundary.test.ts` assertion (no dark selector touches
  a `--venue-*` token) still stands as namespace hygiene.

- **D-11:** **Correct the design project's own positioning statement.** Its
  `readme.md` still opens "One system covers the floor …, the book … and the back
  office, so a small dining room does not need four vendors and a clipboard" —
  verbatim the all-or-nothing suite PROJECT.md names as the competitor gap Cena
  exists to attack. Rewrite it around tiered entry landing on the QR menu. The
  marketing, service and back-office **kits are left untouched** — no roadmap
  phase builds a marketing site. Rationale: that readme is the brief every future
  `/gsd-ui-phase` reads; leaving it wrong mis-briefs every later design pass,
  which is how B-1 entered the system.

- **D-12:** **Take the D-1 archive** into `.planning/design-archive/` before repo
  migration begins — `ui_kits/service/*` (7 files), `ui_kits/back-office/TheBook.jsx`,
  `guidelines/color-service-states.card.html`. The audit calls these "the only
  copy outside claude.ai/design" and the directory still does not exist. Cheap
  insurance against a deletable cloud project. **Defer** the `.design-sync`
  tooling question — its `config.json` targets a deleted project
  (`25b3418f-b297-4143-8bf4-3cf8ef9e05cc`), and what that tooling should do next
  is better decided once the new primitives exist.

- **D-13:** **Fold both parked Phase 01 defects into the 01.1 re-skin plans** —
  G-01-13 (blocker: an EUR venue cannot be created because the last-language
  checkbox is `disabled`, and disabled controls are omitted from `FormData`) in
  `components/venue-form.tsx`, and G-01-14 (major: `createVenue` redirects
  without `revalidatePath`, so the venue switcher is stale after creation) in
  `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` / `VenueSwitcher`. Decided 2026-08-04, resolving
  the open question this file previously left to the planner. Rationale:
  `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` § "Downstream roadmap impact" already argues it — these
  defects "live in the very components 01.1 re-skins. Fixing them separately and
  then re-skinning is duplicate work." **Consequence the plans must absorb:** SC2
  requires the Phase 01 test suite to pass *unchanged*, and this decision moves
  behaviour. Each fix therefore carries its own new regression test, and the
  SC2 invariant is read as "no existing test changes meaning", not "no test is
  added". Both rows must be closed out in `01-UAT.md` when the fixes land.
  — **Reversibility:** reversible — each fix is a small isolated change in a file
  the phase already touches.

- **D-14:** **SC4 stays whole in 01.1 — build the boundary *and* the guardrail,
  seeded with Cena's own pairing as the single member of the curated set.**
  Decided 2026-08-04 alongside the revised D-02. Concretely:
  - Tokens are namespaced **Cena-fixed vs venue-themable** from day one, even
    though nothing consumes the venue half in v1. Retrofitting a namespace later
    means re-cutting every token consumer; doing it now costs almost nothing.
  - The WCAG AA 4.5:1 sweep (`tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts`)
    **ships in 01.1** with Cena's own palette as the only row. It is not vacuous —
    it is a regression guard on Cena's own AA compliance, which
    `color-contrast.card.html` currently proves only by hand. Phase 4 grows it by
    adding rows, not by inventing the mechanism under time pressure.
  - Research's caveat that the sweep is "complete only because D-03 made the
    pairing set finite" still holds; in v1 the set is finite because it has one
    member.
  — **Reversibility:** reversible — the guardrail is additive and the namespace is
  a naming convention, not a data migration.

### Claude's Discretion

None — every area presented was decided explicitly. Where a decision names a
mechanism (subsetting approach, how the contrast guardrail is enforced at the
token boundary), the mechanism itself is left to research and planning.

</decisions>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets

- **Tailwind v4 is already in place** (`tailwindcss ^4`, `@tailwindcss/postcss ^4`)
  and the design system ships `tailwind/cena-theme.css` as a v4 `@theme` block —
  a direct fit, no v3→v4 translation needed.
- **`radix-ui ^1.6.7` + shadcn are already wired** into shipped Phase 01 surfaces
  and are accessible today. Per audit decision D-2, re-skin these rather than
  adopting the design system's hand-rolled JSX primitives, which carry no focus
  management, keyboard nav or ARIA.
- **`lucide-react ^1.27.0` is already a dependency**; the system's 50 glyphs are
  Lucide at 1.75 stroke rather than the stock 2. Adopt the stroke convention
  rather than importing a second icon set.
- **`app/globals.css`** is the single existing token entry point.
- Only **11 primitives exist** today (`alert avatar badge button card checkbox
  dialog dropdown-menu input label sonner`) against the system's **16**. The gap
  — `IconButton`, `Icon`, `Tag`, `Select`, `Radio`, `Switch`, `Field`, `Tabs`,
  `Tooltip`, `Toast` — is net-new work, not re-skinning.

### Established Patterns

- **The Phase 01 test suite is the regression gate.** 46 files / 442 tests green
  as of 2026-08-04. ROADMAP SC2 requires it to pass unchanged through the
  re-skin — behaviour must not move while appearance does.
- **`lib/copy.ts` is the copy deck**, and its house rule is that a user-visible
  string with no Copywriting Contract row is a *signal that the design has no
  screen for that state*, not licence to invent one inline. D-04 works within
  this rule.
- **Server Components by default**; the dashboard layout renders the sidebar,
  nav and venue switcher server-side. Re-skinning must not push these to the
  client.

### Integration Points

- `app/globals.css` → the new token layer (`tokens/*.css` + `cena-theme.css`).
- `components/ui/*` → re-skinned Radix primitives; every consuming surface in
  `app/` and `components/` inherits the change.
- The venue-theme token contract (D-02) is a **new** boundary this phase creates;
  Phase 4's THEME-01..04 is its first consumer, and nothing consumes it in 01.1.

</code_context>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- **Last-good banner wording** (D-07), as discussed: "Saved menu from 14:20.
  Prices and sold-out items may have changed." Treat as the intent, not
  necessarily the final string — it must pass through the D-04 lexicon re-cut and
  land as a Copywriting Contract row.
- **Zero-photo layout** (D-08): dish name in the serif, description, price,
  allergens, generous spacing, and **no image slot at all** — not a wash, not a
  stripe, nothing occupying where a photo would be.
- The design project's `SKILL.md` is an Agent Skills wrapper intended for use in
  Claude Code — worth evaluating as a way for later `/gsd-ui-phase` runs to read
  the system directly rather than via ad-hoc fetches.

</specifics>

## Deferred Ideas

- **Owner/venue UI customization, entire** — the revised D-02 moves all of it out
  of v1. v1 ships one brand: Cena's. THEME-01..04 and the venue theming UI become
  a later milestone. 01.1 still builds the token namespace and the contrast
  guardrail that milestone will consume (D-14), but nothing in v1 reads them.
- **Venue font pairings 2–4** — self-hosting and subsetting for the non-default
  pairings ships with the theming milestone (D-09, D-03).
- **Dark-mode UI** — tokens kept, no surface wired; revisit if a requirement ever
  asks for it (D-10).
- **Marketing site re-author (B-1's kit half)** — the positioning *statement* is
  corrected in 01.1 (D-11), but no phase in the current roadmap builds a
  marketing site.
- **`.design-sync` tooling direction** — its config targets a deleted project;
  decide repoint-vs-retire once the new primitive layer exists (D-12).
- **A real logo / wordmark** — none exists; "Cena" is a type-only wordmark set in
  Newsreader. Not scoped to any phase.
- **THEME-04 contrast-guardrail enforcement mechanism** — the *rule* is locked
  (no venue theme may produce a sub-AA pair); *how* it is enforced at the token
  boundary was not discussed and belongs to Phase 4 planning or 01.1 research.
- **Owner-side patterns** — per-language authoring (LANG-01..04) and the QR print
  sheet (DINE-01) ship with their own phases (D-06).

## Open Question for the Planner — RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (see D-13)

**Do the parked Phase 01 gaps get fixed inside the 01.1 re-skin plans?** **Yes —
both.** Decided at plan-phase dispatch on 2026-08-04 and promoted to **D-13** in
`<decisions>` above, which is the binding record. The discussion that produced
the question is kept below for its detail.

- **G-01-13** (blocker) lives in `components/venue-form.tsx` — an EUR venue
  cannot be created because the last-language checkbox is `disabled`, and
  disabled controls are omitted from `FormData`.
- **G-01-14** (major) lives in `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` / `VenueSwitcher` —
  `createVenue` redirects without `revalidatePath`, so the switcher is stale
  after creation.

Both are `status: parked` in `01-UAT.md` — real defects, consciously carried,
still owed. **`DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` § "Downstream roadmap impact" already argues the
answer**: it notes Phase 01's UAT gaps "live in the very components 01.1
re-skins. Fixing them separately and then re-skinning is duplicate work; fold
them into the 01.1 re-skin plans, or close them before 01.1 starts." That note
was written about G-01-6/G-01-7 (both now closed); the same logic applies
unchanged to G-01-13 and G-01-14. The planner should surface this rather than
silently choosing.

</deferred>
